transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I’m not sure how to explain it without sounding overly sensitive, but for nearly two years I’ve had this feeling—well, more than a feeling—that after a commission I did, a few people in the ensemble started… sort of quietly working against me.

It’s things like schedule changes, where people sit, little comments during rehearsals. They’ll show me emails or notes that are meant to explain it, and I understand how that might look normal, but I still can’t really shake the certainty that there’s something behind it. I know that may sound like I’m reading too much into things, but it’s been hard to get past.
Do you believe that these actions by the ensemble members are intentionally meant to harm or undermine you, even though others might see them as normal or accidental?

I… yes, I suppose that’s the part I’m having trouble saying plainly. I don’t think it’s just accidental, at least not all of it.

I’m here because for almost two years I haven’t been able to shake the certainty that after that commission, a few people in the ensemble started doing things—schedule changes, seating choices, small comments in rehearsals—that were meant to quietly undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it, I can see how it might look normal, but it still feels intentional to me. Does that make sense?
Has this concern about being undermined affected other parts of your life, or is it mainly limited to your experiences with the ensemble?

It’s mostly limited to the ensemble, I think. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like it’s taken over everything.

Outside of that, I’m still functioning pretty normally—I meet my deadlines, I’m composing, I run most mornings, and things at home with my wife are basically steady. So… I guess it’s not affecting every area of my life, if that’s the right way to put it.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially around the time this situation with the ensemble started?

I don’t think so… not in a major way, at least. I mean, I’ve had days where I feel worn out or frustrated by it, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been hopeless or that I stopped enjoying music or running or things like that.

I hope that’s the kind of thing you mean. It’s more that the situation bothers me when it comes up, rather than my whole mood changing, if that makes sense.
Have you ever felt like there were other things happening—things that others don’t seem to notice or agree with—that you just know are true, even if you can’t prove them?

I don’t think there are other things, really… not outside of this. I mean, I know how that sounds, and I’m trying not to make it bigger than it is.

It’s mainly the ensemble situation. For almost two years now, since that commission, I haven’t been able to shake the feeling—well, the certainty, I guess—that a few of them were using things like schedule changes, seating decisions, little rehearsal comments to quietly undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that explain it another way, I can see how someone else would accept that, but I still feel like I know what’s really behind it.

I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Have you ever had beliefs that something was true, even when others could not see it or prove it, in any other parts of your life outside of this ensemble situation?

No, not really… at least, I don’t think so. It’s not like I have a whole set of things like that in other areas.

It’s really this ensemble situation that I keep coming back to. Since that commission, I’ve just been unable to shake the certainty that a few people there were using schedule changes, seating choices, and small comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, I can understand how it looks reasonable to other people… but I still feel like I know what was really happening.

I hope that’s answering it clearly.
Do you believe that these people in the ensemble are working together in a coordinated way to undermine you, even if there’s no direct proof of that?

I wouldn’t want to overstate it, but… yes, that’s how it feels to me. Not like some huge formal plan, maybe, but a few of them seemed to be acting in the same direction after the commission.

It’s the schedule changes, the seating choices, little comments in rehearsals—each thing on its own can be explained away, and they have shown me emails or notes that supposedly explain it. I understand why other people might say, “See, there’s no proof.” But I still can’t shake the certainty that they were quietly trying to undermine my work.

I know that may sound like a lot. I’m just trying to answer honestly.

Even though you understand how others might see the emails and notes as reasonable explanations, do you feel that your belief that they were trying to undermine you is something you just know is true, regardless of what the evidence shows?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t love saying it that strongly, because I know it can sound unreasonable, and I’m not trying to ignore what people show me.

But even when I look at the emails or the notes and I can see how they’re supposed to explain the schedule changes or seating choices or comments, it doesn’t really change what I feel certain about. For almost two years, since that commission, I’ve just felt like a few people in the ensemble were quietly trying to undermine my work.

I know other people may not see it that way, but to me it still feels true.

Even though you’ve seen emails and notes that explain these actions as normal or accidental, do you feel that your belief that they were trying to undermine you is absolutely true, and that no amount of evidence could really change that?

I… yes, I think that’s what I’m trying to say, even if I know it sounds a bit intense.

It’s not that I want to be stubborn or dismissive of the emails and notes. I can see how they explain things on the surface. But for almost two years now, since that commission, I haven’t been able to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble were using the schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work.

I don’t know if I should say “no amount of evidence,” exactly… but honestly, so far nothing they’ve shown me has changed what I feel sure is true. Does that make sense?
Even when presented with clear explanations that contradict your belief, do you still feel certain that these people were trying to undermine you?

Yes… I do. I know that probably isn’t the “right” answer, and I’m not trying to be difficult.

When they show me emails or notes explaining the schedule changes or the seating decisions, I can understand how those explanations sound reasonable. But I still feel certain that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble were using those things—plus the little comments in rehearsals—to quietly undermine my work.

I wish I could just let the explanations settle it, but they don’t, not really.
Has there ever been a time when you questioned your belief about the ensemble trying to undermine you, even briefly, or has it remained completely firm throughout the past two years?

I’ve… I’ve tried to question it, if that makes sense. I know I’m supposed to look at the emails and notes and say, “Okay, maybe it was just a scheduling thing,” or “Maybe the seating choice wasn’t personal.”

And I have had moments where I think, maybe I’m making too much of it, maybe I should just let it go. But those moments don’t really last. Underneath it, I still feel certain that after that commission, a few people in the ensemble were quietly using those changes and comments to undermine my work.

I’m not saying I’m proud of being that sure. I know how it sounds. But no, it hasn’t really gone away.

Even when you’ve tried to question your belief and considered that the explanations provided might be accurate, does your certainty that they were trying to undermine you always come back, or have you ever found a moment where you truly believed it might not be intentional?

I think… it does come back, yes.

I’ve had little moments where I try to be fair and tell myself, maybe the emails are exactly what they say they are, maybe the notes explain it, maybe no one meant anything by the seating or the schedule changes. I do try to consider that, because I don’t want to seem unreasonable.

But I don’t think I’ve ever really believed, deep down, that it wasn’t intentional. Not for more than a moment. It always settles back into this certainty that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble were quietly using those things to undermine my work.

I know that may sound like I’m not being open-minded enough, but that’s honestly how it feels.
Have you ever experienced things like hearing voices, seeing things that others don’t, or having beliefs that others say are completely out of touch with reality?

I haven’t heard voices or seen things, no. Nothing like that.

The main thing is… the belief about the ensemble. I know other people think it’s an overreaction, or that I’m reading too much into normal decisions. But for almost two years I haven’t been able to shake the certainty that after the commission, a few people started using schedule changes, seating choices, and small comments in rehearsal to undermine my work.

Even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it, I can see why those explanations sound reasonable, but I don’t really feel convinced by them. I know that may sound… extreme, but that’s the thing I’m here about.
Even though you’ve seen explanations that go against your belief, do you feel absolutely certain that your view is correct and that nothing could ever convince you otherwise?

I wouldn’t want to say nothing could ever convince me otherwise, because that sounds… I don’t know, too rigid. I do try to listen when people show me emails or rehearsal notes, and I can understand that they’re meant to explain the schedule changes or seating decisions.

But if I’m being honest, I’m still very sure. For almost two years I haven’t been able to shake the feeling that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble were using those changes and little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work.

I know that may not be the answer I’m supposed to give, but… yes, my certainty keeps coming back.
